Frost, or 27 miles east of Fairmont, moving northeast at 30 mph.

Elmore, Alden, Emmons, Bricelyn, Hartland, Freeborn, Mansfield,
Easton, Frost, Delavan, Twin Lakes, Conger, Kiester and Granada.

events.title: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.region: Dare, NC
events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
At 440 AM EDT, Doppler radar indicated thunderstorms produced heavy
rain across the warned area. Between 4 and 7 inches of rain have
fallen. Additional rainfall amounts up to 0.5 inches are possible in
the warned area. Flash flooding is ongoing or expected to begin
shortly.

HAZARD...Flash flooding caused by thunderstorms.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Flash flooding of small creeks and streams, urban areas,
highways, streets and underpasses as well as other poor
drainage and low-lying areas.

Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Rodanthe, Waves, Salvo and Hatteras Island Fishing Pier.

NC 12 near Pea Island National Wildlife Refuge is prone to flooding.
Areas of deep water on the road may be difficult to see in the dark.

* WHEN...Until 600 AM EDT.

* IMPACTS...Minor flooding in low-lying and poor drainage areas.

events.region: Jenkins; Screven; Candler; Bulloch; Tattnall; Evans; Allendale; Hampton; Inland Colleton; Dorchester; Inland Berkeley
events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
Areas of fog will impact interior portions of the South Carolina
Lowcountry and Southeast Georgia through daybreak. The fog could
become locally dense at times with visibilities 1/4 mile or less. The
nature of the fog is such that visibilities will vary greatly over
short distances with the risk for locally dense fog being the
greatest near bodies of water and other low-lying areas such as
marshes, swamps and large ditches. Motorists should remain alert for
these conditions this morning. Conditions will quickly improve after
daybreak.

events.title: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.region: Western Columbia River Gorge in Oregon and Washington
events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
...CRITICAL FIRE WEATHER CONDITIONS EXPECTED IN THE WESTERN
COLUMBIA RIVER GORGE THIS AFTERNOON THROUGH WEDNESDAY EVENING FOR
DRY CONDITIONS AND EASTERLY WINDS UP TO 38 MPH...

* AFFECTED AREA...In Washington, Fire Weather Zone 636 Western
Columbia River Gorge in Oregon and Washington.

* WINDS...East 10 to 20 mph with gusts up to 38 mph. Winds will
be strongest this morning through the early afternoon, and again
tonight through early Wednesday afternoon.

* RELATIVE HUMIDITY...As low as 15-20 percent. Relative humidity
values will be lowest this afternoon and Wednesday afternoon.
Poor overnight humidity recoveries are expected with maximum
relative humidity values ranging between 35-45%.

* IMPACTS...Conditions may be favorable for rapid fire spread
which may threaten life and property. Use extra caution with
potential ignition sources, especially in grassy areas.
Outdoor burning is not recommended.
